 Order

This first application has been filed by applicant under Section 483 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 for grant of bail in connection with Crime No. 110/2023 registered at Police Station- Chimanganj Mandi, District Ujjain, (M.P.) for offence punishable under Sections 363, 366, 376,
376(2)(l), 376(3) ,344 of IPC and Sections 5(l), 6 of POCSO Act,
The applicant is in judicial custody since 13.02.2025.
Learned Counsel for the applicant submits that the victim has left her parental home and went with the applicant at her own.
It is a case of romantic relationship between two young persons.
They had married at Morvi Gujarat.
Thereafter one and a half year ago, they went to Indore, where the applicant started working as Delivery Boy.
They have been blessed with a daughter.
When victim was informed by her uncle about the complaint made by her father.
She and the applicant appeared before P.S.- Chimanganj Mandi.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:9751 2 MCRC-11594-2025 Learned counsel referred to the statement of victim recorded u/s 183 of BNSS, 2023 submits that the victim wish to live with the applicant.
The applicant is aged 22 years at present.
He is a labourer by profession and the sole bread earner of his family.
Applicant may be extended the benefit of bail.

sentences.text: Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent/State opposes the bail application on the ground of gravity of alleged offence and cites criminal antecedent of 01 case against the applicant.
In reply, learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant stand acquitted vide judgment dated 10.03.2022 passed in S.C. No. 49/2021.
Heard the arguments, perused the grounds for grant of bail stated in the application and the case diary.
Allegedly, the applicant kidnapped and committed penetrative sexual assault on the minor victim.
It appears that the victim did not support the prosecution.
The applicant and the victim stayed together for almost two years and blessed with a daughter.
The veracity of the prosecution and the age of the victim will be determined after evidence by the trial Court.
As informed, applicant is aged around 22 years.
He is labourer by profession and is the sole bread earner of his family.

In absence of any substantial criminal past and previous conviction for any major offence, considering the socio- economic status of the applicant, there appears to be no likelihood of tampering with evidence by the applicant.
The trial would take time to conclude.
There appears to be no compelling reason to continue incarceration of the applicant.
However, the observations, herein-above, are recorded for present application only.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:9751 3 MCRC-11594-2025

Considering the rival contentions and overall circumstances of the case, in the light of aforesaid facts, but without commenting on the merits, this Court is inclined to release the applicant on bail.
Thus, present application is allowed.

Accordingly, it is directed that applicant - Kamal shall be released on bail in connection with the crime as stated in para-1 of this order, upon furnishing personal bond and surety bond of amount, as may be considered appropriate by the Trial Court for compliance with conditions, as may be imposed by such Court under Section 437(3) of Cr.P.C. 1973/ Section 480(3) of BNSS, 2023, to secure presence of the applicant for the trial.
This order shall be effective till the end of trial.
However, in case of breach of any of the preconditions of bail, the Trial Court may consider, on merit, cancellation of bail without any impediment of this order.
The concerned Court shall get the conditions reproduced on the personal bond by the accused and on surety bond by the surety concerned.
If any of them is unable to write, the scribe shall certify that he had explained the conditions to the concerned accused or the surety.
C.C. as per rules.
